title: The Brunies halfway house as an early nightclub
summary: He locates the halfway house, calls it one of the first New Orleans nightclubs, and says Abbey's band was strictly Dixieland.

story.theme_name: Gangsters, bootleggers and rough clubs of Prohibition
story.community_name: Cabarets, honky-tonks and the Storyville nightlife scene

blocks.x: Did you know Georgie? I guess he got nothing else.
No I didn't. I didn't know Georgie Bruny's. I knew Abby, but I didn't know Georgie.
And where did you say Abby's played?
And where's that? That's where the Orkin place is now?
They used to call it Chris's now.

I don't know what they got there now. I think it's torn down. They had to tear down and come through there with that street. Yeah. They made that overpass there and that underpass. Uh-huh. You know where the new basin was. Yeah I know where it is. Right where the new bridge used to go over the new basin. Metry Road and the new basin.
What kind of band was that? Oh they had a good band. Abby had a good band on them. Yeah.
What did you call it a, was it Dixieland or was it Arrangements? Dixieland.

They played nice stuff man. They used to, that's one of the first night clubs they had in New Orleans. They came, you never had all these clubs then you know. Uh-huh. They were the only place I knew of outside of Bucktown. You could go to Bucktown and go to one of these night clubs. Brunens had a night club out there but that was a different Brunens than the musicians you're speaking of.
